items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to directing the public service commission to conduct an in-depth public interest analysis of proposed mergers by telephone corporations and other telecommunications services providers over which said commission has jurisdiction
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4888

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public service law, in relation to
directing the public service commission to conduct an in-depth public
interest analysis of proposed mergers by telephone corporations and
other telecommunications services providers over which said commission
has jurisdiction

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  This bill would require closer scruti-
ny of proposed telecommunications industry transfers of control, and
declares that except where the public interest requires a contrary
result, a portion of the benefits of such mergers should be returned to
the state's ratepayers.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:  This law would amend section 99 and
section 100 of the public service law.

JUSTIFICATION:  The public interest requires that the Public Service
Commission's analysis of mergers and conclusions drawn there from arise
from objective and verifiable empirical evidence, rather than from
unsupported statements of policy or observations. It is additionally in
the public interest to require a portion of the benefits of telecommuni-
cations mergers to be returned to the state's ratepayers as refunds,
reinvestment in the infrastructure providing E-911 services, or to
finance repairs, maintenance or new construction that might otherwise be
unfunded. Finally, requiring the Public Service Commission to conduct
its analysis upon an enumerated list of public interest factors
increases the participation of the public and other stakeholder groups
in such proceedings, which enhances the transparency and accountability
of the merger analysis process.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  Senate: This is a New Bill

Assembly:

A.6248 of 2013-14; A.6450 of 2011-12 - In Corporations A.2208d -
2009/2010 Passed Assembly.  A.9809 (2006) A.10043 (2007-2008)

FISCAL IMPACT:  None

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect 120 days after it shall have
become law, and any rule or regulation necessary for the timely imple-
mentation of this act on its effective date shall be promulgated imme-
diately.

C.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to creating standards by which the public service commission reviews and approves a merger or acquisition between telephone corporations, cable corporations, and combination telephone and cable corporations
C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4888C

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to creating
standards by which the public service commission reviews and approves
a merger or acquisition between telephone corporations, cable
corporations, and combination telephone and cable corporations

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

This bill would create new standards by which the Public Service
Commission reviews and approves a merger or acquisition between
telephone corporations, cable corporations, and combination telephone
and cable corporations.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

*Section one of the bill:

o requires review and consent of the Public Service Commission to
certain proposed mergers
o applies higher scrutiny of mergers only to companies with gross
annual revenues of $100 million or more;
o establishes threshold public interest standards to be utilized by
the public service commission during its review of the merger;
o mandates consideration of reasonable alternatives or modifications
to the proposed merger;
o requires the creation of a specific program where services for
low-income individuals are offered at reasonable rates;
o clarifies that the applicants have the burden of proving by a
preponderance of evidence their compliance with the required public
interest threshold standards;
o formulates the method for determining annual revenues of the
applicants;
o requires the commission to issue a finding of fact regarding their
review and determinations;
o requires a full evidentiary hearing; and,
o clarifies that review and consent required by this section does not
necessarily impact review or consent required by any other section
law.

*Section two of the bill is a severability clause

*Section three of the bill is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Over the last two decades, traditional telephone and cable
corporations have begun to offer cable, broadband, and telephone
services. Increasingly, policymakers are realizing there is a strong
need for universal access to high speed broadband and are adopting
measures to reach increased access. At the same time, this industry is
experiencing a rapid trend of consolidation. In response to the
consolidation of telephone and cable corporations, the laws governing
the review and approval of these transactions should be modernized.
This bill would create an enhanced review process to insure that the
public interest is protected when an acquisition or merger is proposed
that involves telephone, cable, or combination telephone and cable
corporations.

The public interest standard developed in this bill would require
Public Service Commission approval to be based on objective and
verifiable empirical evidence, rather than from unsupported statements
of policy or unsubstantiated observations. This public interest
standard would require that customers receive verifiable benefits such
as reinvestment and improvement of a corporation's offerings or the
creation of a program offering services to low income customers at
reduced rates. It would also require the Public Service. Commission to
conduct its review with the participation of the public and other
stakeholder groups in a transparent manner.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

Senate: This is a New Bill

Assembly:

A.6248 of 2013-14; A.6450 of 2011-12 - In Corporations A.2208d
2009/2010 Passed Assembly, A.9809 (2006) A.10043 (2007-2008)

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Some costs related to administrative work of the Department of Public
Service.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Creates standards by which the public service commission reviews and approves a merger or acquisition between telephone corporations, cable corporations and combination telephone and cable corporations.
